def test_refused_current_entry_preserves_all_foreign_entries(self) -> None:
        self.mkdir(*TOOL_DIRS.values())
        entries = {"owner-chat": {"command": "/owner/hosted"},
                   "simple-chat": {"command": "/owner/custom"}}
        self.write(".config/muse/settings.json", json.dumps({"mcpServers": entries}))
        self.run_cli("apply", "muse", "--with-simple-chat")
        self.assertEqual({key: self.load(".config/muse/settings.json")["mcpServers"][key] for key in entries}, entries)

foreign = current.replace("mcp-simple-chat", "mcp-owner-chat")
        self.write(path, current + foreign)
        self.run_cli("apply", "clutch", "--with-simple-chat", "--no-dsh-check")
        self.assertIn(foreign, self.read(path))
        self.assertEqual(self.read(path).count("fleet:begin mcp-simple-chat"), 1)
        self.run_cli("remove", "clutch", "--with-simple-chat", "--no-dsh-check")
        self.assertIn(foreign, self.read(path))

# of the three markers that matter is enough on its own, which is what exercises the SIMPLE_TOOLS_ATTACH=0 line.

class RegistryRemoteTests(Base):
    """LETTER_REGISTRY_REMOTE:  the registry host named outright, decoupled from where the chat runs.

A Mac chat (platform darwin, no location override) registers locally while no destination is
    named, and over the hop once one is:  the destination wins, a failure of it is an error answer
    and never a quiet local write, and this host keeps no registry file of its own."""

env = self.env(**extra)
        code = CL.hook(env, io.StringIO(json.dumps(payload)), out, runner=runner, platform="darwin")

text = out.getvalue().strip()
        return json.loads(text)["hookSpecificOutput"] if text else None

def test_a_mac_session_registers_over_the_hop_and_keeps_no_local_file(self) -> None:
        ssh = self.RemoteSsh(self)
        out = self.start("a-0001", ssh, LETTER_REGISTRY_REMOTE="registry-host")
        self.assertEqual(ssh.ops(), ["register"])
        rec = self.remote_lookup("a-0001")
        self.assertIsNotNone(rec)
        self.assertIsNone(self.remote_lookup("a-0001", location="server"),
                          "the location stays where the session runs")
        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.db), "no local registry file is created")

def test_a_mac_session_without_the_setting_registers_locally_as_before(self) -> None:
        OR.SessionRegistry(self.db).close_db()  # the Mac's registry exists, as it does today
        ssh = self.RemoteSsh(self, fail=AssertionError("the hop must not be tried"))
        out = self.start("a-0002", ssh)
        self.assertEqual(ssh.calls, [])
        self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(self.db), "the Mac-local registry is used")
        reg = OR.SessionRegistry(self.db)
        try:
            self.assertIsNotNone(reg.lookup(CL.PLATFORM, "mac", CL.SCOPE, "a-0002"))
        finally:
            reg.close_db()

def test_a_failed_hop_is_an_error_answer_and_never_a_local_fallback(self) -> None:
        ssh = self.RemoteSsh(self, fail=OSError("no route"))
        out = self.start("a-0003", ssh, LETTER_REGISTRY_REMOTE="registry-host")
        self.assertEqual(ssh.ops(), ["register"])
        self.assertIn("No Operator letter yet", (out or {}).get("additionalContext", ""))
        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.db), "a failed hop never becomes a local write")
        self.assertIsNone(self.remote_lookup("a-0003"))

def test_a_destination_that_is_not_plain_is_refused_by_its_own_name(self) -> None:
        ssh = self.RemoteSsh(self, fail=AssertionError("a refused destination is never run"))
        out = self.start("a-0004", ssh, LETTER_REGISTRY_REMOTE="-oProxyCommand=touch /tmp/x")
        self.assertEqual(ssh.calls, [])
        self.assertIn("LETTER_REGISTRY_REMOTE does not name an ssh destination",
                      (out or {}).get("additionalContext", ""))
        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(self.db))

    def test_the_parent_is_resolved_where_the_app_record_is(self) -> None:
        # Chat A is started on this Mac;  the desktop app then starts chat B from A.  The registry
        # host holds no copy of the app's records, so the hook names the parent it resolved here.
        from simple_tools.tests.test_claude_app_lineage import write as write_app_record

        write_app_record(self.home, "local_11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
                         {"cliSessionId": "33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333"})
        write_app_record(self.home, "local_22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222",
                         {"cliSessionId": "44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444",
                          "spawnedFrom": {"sessionId": "local_11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
                                          "title": "t", "handOff": True}})
        ssh = self.RemoteSsh(self)
        self.start("33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333", ssh,
                   LETTER_REGISTRY_REMOTE="registry-host",
                   CLAUDE_CODE_HOST_SESSION_ID="local_11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111")
        self.start("44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444", ssh,
                   LETTER_REGISTRY_REMOTE="registry-host",
                   CLAUDE_CODE_HOST_SESSION_ID="local_22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222")
        self.assertEqual(ssh.ops(), ["register", "register"])
        argv = shlex.split(ssh.calls[1][8])
        self.assertIn("--parent-session-id=33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333", argv)
        child = self.remote_lookup("44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444")
        self.assertIsNotNone(child)
        parent = self.remote_lookup("33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333")
        self.assertEqual(child["label"][0], parent["label"][0], "the child takes the parent's pair")

    def test_the_operator_service_identity_loads_from_its_own_project(self) -> None:
        ops = {
            "ZULIP_OPERATOR_EMAIL": "operator-bot@zulip.test",
            "ZULIP_OPERATOR_API_KEY": "zk-" + secrets.token_hex(12),
            "OPERATOR_ZULIP_USER_ID": "1217148",
            "OPERATOR_ZULIP_EMAIL": "operator-bot@zulip.test",
            "ZULIP_CLAUDE_API_KEY": "not-the-operator-folder's-name",  # not a service name:  dropped here
        }
        with FakeInfisical(self.cid, self.csecret, self.values, operator=ops) as fake:
            out, line = IE.operator_service_identity(self.env(fake, INFISICAL_FLEET_OPS_PROJECT_ID=self.FLEET_OPS, INFISICAL_OPERATOR_VOICE_TOKEN=fake.pin))
        for name in ("OPERATOR_ZULIP_USER_ID", "OPERATOR_ZULIP_EMAIL"):
            self.assertEqual(out[name], ops[name], "%s comes from the Fleet-OPS folder" % name)
        # The credential pair is NEVER injected into the environment, even though the folder
        # carries it:  the Operator's credentials reach the daemon only through the
        # scoped-service-token reader, per the owner's clarified normal method.
        self.assertNotIn("ZULIP_OPERATOR_EMAIL", out)
        self.assertNotIn("ZULIP_OPERATOR_API_KEY", out)
        self.assertNotIn("ZULIP_CLAUDE_API_KEY", out, "the helper returns only service pins")
        self.assertIn("Operator service identity from /zulip_operator: 2 of 2", line)
        reads = self.operator_folder_reads(fake)
        self.assertEqual(len(reads), 1)
        self.assertIn("workspaceId=%s" % self.FLEET_OPS, reads[0])
        for value in ops.values():
            self.assertNotIn(value, line)

    def test_a_folder_pin_that_disagrees_with_the_host_pin_is_refused(self) -> None:
        ops = {
            "ZULIP_OPERATOR_EMAIL": "operator-bot@zulip.test",
            "ZULIP_OPERATOR_API_KEY": "zk-" + secrets.token_hex(12),
            "OPERATOR_ZULIP_USER_ID": "1217148",
            "OPERATOR_ZULIP_EMAIL": "other-bot@zulip.test",
        }
        env = self.env  # bound before the with, for readability below
        with FakeInfisical(self.cid, self.csecret, self.values, operator=ops) as fake:
            out, line = IE.operator_service_identity(env(fake, INFISICAL_FLEET_OPS_PROJECT_ID=self.FLEET_OPS, INFISICAL_OPERATOR_VOICE_TOKEN=fake.pin,
                                         OPERATOR_ZULIP_EMAIL="operator-bot@zulip.test"))
        self.assertNotIn("OPERATOR_ZULIP_USER_ID", out, "both pins are refused on a disagreement")
        self.assertNotIn("OPERATOR_ZULIP_EMAIL", out, "the conflicting folder cannot override the host")
        self.assertNotIn("ZULIP_OPERATOR_API_KEY", out, "the pair never loads, pin or no pin")
        self.assertIn("Operator service pins refused (folder pin disagrees with the host pin)", line)
        self.assertNotIn(ops["ZULIP_OPERATOR_API_KEY"], line)
        self.assertNotIn("other-bot@zulip.test", line)

    def test_the_operator_credential_pair_is_never_injected(self) -> None:
        # Even with no pins anywhere, the folder's credential pair does not enter the
        # environment:  no Zulip key pair rides env on the normal service-token path.
        ops = {
            "ZULIP_OPERATOR_EMAIL": "someone-else@zulip.test",
            "ZULIP_OPERATOR_API_KEY": "zk-" + secrets.token_hex(12),
        }
        with FakeInfisical(self.cid, self.csecret, self.values, operator=ops) as fake:
            out, line = IE.operator_service_identity(self.env(fake, INFISICAL_FLEET_OPS_PROJECT_ID=self.FLEET_OPS, INFISICAL_OPERATOR_VOICE_TOKEN=fake.pin))
        self.assertNotIn("ZULIP_OPERATOR_API_KEY", out)
        self.assertNotIn("ZULIP_OPERATOR_EMAIL", out)
        self.assertNotIn(ops["ZULIP_OPERATOR_API_KEY"], line)
        self.assertNotIn("someone-else@zulip.test", line)

    def test_a_non_numeric_operator_user_id_is_refused_alone(self) -> None:
        ops = {
            "ZULIP_OPERATOR_EMAIL": "operator-bot@zulip.test",
            "ZULIP_OPERATOR_API_KEY": "zk-" + secrets.token_hex(12),
            "OPERATOR_ZULIP_USER_ID": "not-a-number",
            "OPERATOR_ZULIP_EMAIL": "operator-bot@zulip.test",

        with FakeInfisical(self.cid, self.csecret, self.values, operator=ops) as fake:
            out, line = IE.operator_service_identity(self.env(fake, INFISICAL_FLEET_OPS_PROJECT_ID=self.FLEET_OPS, INFISICAL_OPERATOR_VOICE_TOKEN=fake.pin))
        self.assertNotIn("OPERATOR_ZULIP_USER_ID", out)
        self.assertNotIn("ZULIP_OPERATOR_API_KEY", out, "the pair never loads")
        self.assertIn("OPERATOR_ZULIP_USER_ID refused (not a positive id)", line)
